title: Why Did Jesus Call Himself “The Son of Man”? The Hidden Identity That Changes Everything You Thought You Knew About Christ
paragraphs:
Why Did Jesus Call Himself “The Son of Man”? The Hidden Identity That Changes Everything You Thought You Knew About Christ
The title everyone overlooked… the prophecy everyone missed… and the reason Jesus chose these words may completely transform how you see your Savior forever.
If you were trying to convince the world that you truly were the promised Messiah, these are probably the titles you would repeat over and over again.
More than any other title, He consistently called Himself something that sounds surprisingly ordinary.
To many modern readers, it almost sounds humble... perhaps even weaker.
Some assume Jesus was simply emphasizing His humanity.
Others think He was avoiding openly claiming to be God.
But neither explanation comes close to revealing the breathtaking depth hidden inside these three words.
In reality, every time Jesus called Himself "the Son of Man," He was declaring something so profound that many of His listeners immediately understood exactly what He meant.
And unless we understand why Jesus loved this title so much, we may miss one of the greatest revelations in the entire Gospel.
This is not merely a study of biblical terminology.
This is the story of the God who stepped into humanity—not simply to visit us, but to rescue us.
Because from scandal to grace, Jesus rewrites everything.
The first time Scripture introduces the expression "son of man," it simply refers to a human being.
In Hebrew, the expression is בֶּן־אָדָם (ben-'adam).
Throughout the Old Testament, especially in the book of Ezekiel, God repeatedly addresses the prophet as:
"Son of man, stand upon thy feet, and I will speak unto thee."
Here, the phrase emphasizes human weakness compared to God's infinite majesty.
Ezekiel is reminded that he is merely human.
But when Jesus uses the title...
Because He isn't merely borrowing Ezekiel's title.
Centuries before Christ was born, the prophet Daniel witnessed one of the greatest prophetic scenes in all of Scripture.

"I saw in the night visions, and behold, with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man, and he came to the Ancient of Days and was presented before Him. And to Him was given dominion and glory and a kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve Him; His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away."
He comes with the clouds of heaven.
Throughout Scripture, riding upon the clouds is something uniquely associated with God Himself (Psalm 104:3; Isaiah 19:1).
Then Daniel says all nations worship and serve Him.
The Aramaic verb פְּלַח (pelach) is especially significant because elsewhere in Daniel it refers to the worship or service due to God alone (Daniel 3:12, 17–18, 28; 6:16, 20).
This "Son of Man" receives everlasting dominion, universal authority, and divine worship.
He is fully distinct from the Ancient of Days, yet He shares divine authority.
Over eighty times in the Gospels.
Jesus was quietly pointing every attentive listener back to Daniel's heavenly vision.
The eternal King Daniel saw before history unfolded.
This becomes unmistakably clear during Jesus' trial.
Standing before the high priest, Jesus is asked directly:
"Are You the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed?"
ἐγώ εἰμι· καὶ ὄψεσθε τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου (ton Huion tou Anthrōpou) καθήμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς Δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
"I am. And you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven."
The high priest tears his garments.
Because everyone in that courtroom understood what Jesus had just claimed.
He identified Himself as Daniel's divine Son of Man.
That is why they accused Him of blasphemy.
Not because He claimed to be merely human.
Because He claimed equality with God.
Ironically, the title many people think sounds modest is actually one of Jesus' clearest messianic and divine self-identifications.
Yet the wonder of this title goes even deeper.
The Son of Man is not only the glorious King of Daniel.
He is also the suffering Servant.
Jesus repeatedly connects "the Son of Man" with His coming death.
ὁ γὰρ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου (ho gar Huios tou Anthrōpou) οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
"For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many."
The One Daniel saw receiving everlasting worship...
The One seated beside the Ancient of Days...
The Creator stepped into His own creation.
The King accepted a criminal's cross.
This is why the Gospel is unlike any other story ever told.
Every other religion tells humanity how to climb toward God.
The Gospel tells us God climbed down toward humanity.

Though existing in the form of God, Christ humbled Himself, taking the form of a servant and becoming obedient unto death—even death on a cross. Because of this, God highly exalted Him and bestowed on Him the name above every name, so that every knee should bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
The Son of Man embraces both unimaginable humility and infinite majesty.
He alone bridges heaven and earth.
He alone can represent humanity before God because He became truly human.
He alone can save humanity because He is truly God.
Without His humanity, He could not stand in our place.
Without His deity, His sacrifice could never cover the sins of the world.
This is why Hebrews calls Him our great High Priest.
He understands every tear you've cried.
Every prayer whispered into the darkness.
Every fear you've hidden behind a smile.
Yet unlike every other human who has ever lived, He defeated death itself.
This is the beauty hidden inside the title "Son of Man."
It reminds us that God did not save us from a distance.
And He still invites every weary soul to come to Him today.
Perhaps you've carried shame for years.
Perhaps your past feels louder than your future.
Perhaps you believe your failures have written the final chapter of your story.
Because Jesus is the Son of Man foretold by Daniel, crucified for sinners, risen in victory, and reigning forever, your identity no longer has to be defined by your worst moment.
That is the heartbeat of the Gospel.

If this message has strengthened your faith or helped you see Jesus more clearly, don't let it stop with you. One of the simplest ways to glorify God is to faithfully steward the truth He has entrusted to you. Your testimony may become the encouragement that leads another person to seek Jesus.
One faithful decision to spread God's truth today may become someone else's first step toward eternity tomorrow.
